# 3D picture native reference

Original OPC/XML and four-color PNG fixture generated by
`tools/canvas_picture_3d_fixture.py`, reusing only our original image pixels.
Thirteen anchored pictures compare orthographic front, perspective right without
extrusion, right with 20pt extrusion, an elliptical right picture with 4.5pt
contour, double dimensions, perspective left, contour-only ellipse, extrusion-only ellipse and a rectangular
contour, flat perspective/orthographic ellipses, and orthographic ellipse/rectangle
contours. The last four cases separate ellipse boundaries and contour effects
from extrusion and perspective. Each anchor starts at
(100pt, 140pt), with 40pt effect extents, on its own page.

The exact source was opened in the reference application with the required
reference-application helper and exported without saving. The generator explicitly supplies the
required settings zoom percentage. `native.pdf` captures all thirteen pages;
`reference.json` records the source SHA-256, 117 outline cross-sections and
52 front-face RGB samples, six interior side-wall samples and 20 contour
samples. Reproduce
measurements with `tools/picture_3d_reference.py`.
`native-properties.json` records automation-API Shape.ThreeD values from the same open
fixture: rotations, field of view, depth, contour, camera, lighting and material.
The reference application exposes right/left as RotationX approximately +20/-20 degrees, zero Y/Z,
45-degree field of view, lighting enum 13 and material enum 8. The interpretation
of those COM axes must be checked against the rendered picture, not assumed.

Relevant ECMA-376 Part 1 clauses: 20.1.5.5 camera, 20.1.5.12 sp3d,
20.1.10.47 preset camera types, and 20.1.4.1.26 scene3d. The preset tables give
illustrations, not a complete numerical rendering algorithm.
Published Open Specifications support material also documents perspective camera distance
as 6.28 / tan(FOV/2) in scene units, an FOV clamp and camera nudging for geometry
behind the camera:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-my/answers/questions/769795/how-to-get-distance-of-view-point-to-xy-plane-for
The camera magnitude mapped through inches to points matches all five rectangular
non-contour cases within 0.75pt on interior/outside scan rows. These cover both
turn directions, two physical sizes and extrusion. See drawing-3d-geometry.test.js.
The silhouette extractor includes dark neutral faces (minimum RGB below 240),
not only saturated colors. Contour geometry remains unresolved.

The original lighting implementation uses the published three-point light rig
and warm matte material from MS-OI29500 sections 2.1.1274(c) and 2.1.1334(b),
including the corrected scene-vector transform. All 58 color samples match
within three RGB levels per channel using Phong shading on encoded channels.
The side-wall samples also distinguish the reference application's independent specular evaluation
from suppressing specular whenever diffuse incidence is negative. No measured
color substitutions or fitted coefficients are used. This is a bounded color
comparison with the reference application's rasterized PDF, not proof of identical rasterization.
Primary source:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/1fd4a662-8623-49c0-82f0-18fa91b413b8

The retained-picture renderer now imports these three cameras, rectangular and
elliptical extrusion, and unlit contours. Surrounding text remains editable;
the original picture XML, relationships and media remain atomic and unchanged.
Other cameras, lighting/material combinations, bevels, frame transforms, grouped
3D pictures and ordinary visible picture outlines remain guarded. The corpus
card still needs the ordinary outline that accompanies each photograph's contour.

Rectangle and elliptical-cylinder intersection tests verify geometry independently.
Exact top/bottom raster boundary rows are excluded from analytic rectangle
intersection comparisons because those sample PDF antialiasing outside the solid.

The flat orthographic ellipse still has a wider raster silhouette than the exact
analytic ellipse (about 0.75–1.375pt on the measured rows using the existing
minimum-RGB threshold). Thus the discrepancy also occurs without extrusion or
perspective. Some of this is the raster edge fringe, so it must not be turned
into a fitted ellipse-size correction. Contour-only cases isolate the additional
effect; simple expansion of both ellipse axes by contour width does not yet
establish fidelity. The painter instead strokes projected front/back boundaries
at the physical contour width, with round joins and visible rectangular side
connections. The front face shifts backward by half the contour width. This
construction is checked against the separate native contour cases.

All 20 contour samples equal the original contour RGB (32,32,96) exactly,
across orthographic/perspective cameras, rectangles/ellipses and zero/nonzero
extrusion. The reference application does not apply the photograph's warm-matte lighting to these
contours. Applying the face shader would be a visible error.

The browser regression checks all face, wall and interior contour colors within
four RGB levels and compares full silhouettes within 1.25pt in both directions.
Boundary extraction includes row and column extrema: row-only samples leave
large gaps along almost-horizontal edges. Euclidean boundary distances avoid
the misleading x-distance on near-tangent scan rows. The reference retains
the original scan rows as well. Contour color samples sit inside the stroke,
away from its antialiased outer edge. These are bounded raster comparisons,
not a claim of pixel-identical output. The test also covers surrounding edits,
export/reopen and exact ZIP-entry undo; internal picture mutations stay guarded.

The browser-edited export was additionally opened in the reference application and
exported back to PDF: thirteen pages, thirteen pictures and the edited text were
confirmed. At 2x resolution every picture region matched the original native reference PDF
exactly (maximum channel difference zero on all thirteen pages). This verifies
preservation by serialization; it does not claim the browser's raster is identical.
